6. Runtime errors

Say you're on call this week. At 3 a.m. a pipeline that was "correct" crashes on a row nobody expected, and you're the one it pages. A pipeline that quietly writes a wrong number instead is worse: nobody gets paged at all. Some operations can fail in DataFusion, and some silently give a wrong answer:
operation what goes wrong
❌ error integer / or % by zero the query fails
❌ error -9223372036854775808 / -1 the result doesn't fit in 64 bits; the query fails
❌ error CAST(x AS BIGINT) of NaN, ±∞ or a huge double (also after ROUND) the query fails
❌ error integer POWER with a negative exponent or a huge result the query fails
❌ error a regular expression that doesn't compile the query fails
❌ error truncating a timestamp near the ends of its range to a month or year DataFusion panics or returns garbage
⚠️ warning +, -, * leaving 64 bits DataFusion wraps around silently: 2⁶² + 2⁶² gives -2⁶³
Lean's model computes with exact (unbounded) integers, and SubstraitLean/Safety.lean lists, for every operation of a plan, which of these can happen. Theorem Rel.mayIssues_sound proves the list complete: if the report lists no error, no input can trigger one. @sv.transform refuses a transformation that may fail, even with no postconditions at all.

Guards, and where DataFusion respects them

The usual fix is a guard: make sure the divisor isn't zero before dividing. Whether a guard works depends on when DataFusion evaluates each part, and that is less obvious than it looks. The table below has a row for each kind of trouble: a zero divisor, MIN divided by -1, and doubles a BIGINT can't hold. Pick a variant, and we'll show Lean's report next to DataFusion actually running it on that table.

data.text/markdown:
What the variants show:
  • nullif(n, 0) and CASE are reliable guards: DataFusion evaluates a CASE branch only when its condition holds, and NULLIF is a CASE underneath. Lean evaluates each branch knowing its condition.
  • A filter below a projection works too: the projection only sees rows that passed. But n != 0 doesn't rule out MIN / -1, so division still may overflow; n > 0 fixes that.
  • The same AND is not a guard: DataFusion may evaluate both sides of an AND, so qty % n runs on the n = 0 row anyway.
  • An earlier filter is not a guard either, which surprises everyone: DataFusion's optimizer merges the two filters into one AND. Lean models that (Rel.loose), so it reports the error, and DataFusion indeed fails.
  • round(amount) becomes a cast to BIGINT, which fails on 1e30 and NaN. Bounding amount first makes it safe, because ROUND is exact and monotone in the model (FloatCode.round_mono).
  • qty + 1 only warns: on MAX it wraps around to MIN. No error, but not the mathematical answer either.

Contracts refuse possible errors

For whoever is on call, this is the part that matters: a contracted transformation must be proved free of runtime errors, not only correct when it runs. Warnings (wrap-around) don't block it:

Report.errors and Report.warnings list the issues; Report.proved is true only when every postcondition is proved and there are no errors. What's trusted here is the timing: when DataFusion evaluates an expression (lazy CASE, eager AND/OR, merged filters). The test suite runs DataFusion and DuckDB on random data, including the extreme values, and checks that they only ever fail where Lean reported an error. You can now tell a guard that works from one that only looks like it, and a contract refuses any plan that could crash, so the 3 a.m. page for a zero divisor never comes. Next up: Windows and ASOF joins, where each row looks at its neighbours.
